title: Calling Methods & Scope
summary: Understand execution control transfer: jumping from caller to callee, argument passing, and returning to the caller.
learningOutcomes: Trace program flow across multiple method boundaries
Nest and chain method calls cleanly
Understand control transfer between caller and callee

activities.title: Core Mechanics: Calling Methods & Scope

breakdown.whatIsIt: Comprehensive exploration of Calling Methods & Scope in Java.
breakdown.whyItMatters: Crucial for writing maintainable, reusable, and bug-free Java applications.
howItWorks: Decomposes complex logic into self-contained subprograms.
Allocates local variables on Call Stack frames.
Passes arguments by value, copying parameter data into frames.
Returns execution control back to caller upon reaching return statement.
keyTakeaways: Mastering Calling Methods & Scope is essential for Java placement interviews and clean architecture.
Methods enforce the DRY principle by eliminating redundant duplicate code.
Parameters act as local placeholders; arguments provide runtime values.
Always consider edge cases such as invalid input parameters or stack overflow.

activities.title: Verified Java Implementation: Calling Methods & Scope
activities.description: Trace how execution flows from main into step1, which calls step2, before returning back.

questions.prompt: What happens to the caller method while the callee method is executing?
options: The caller method is destroyed from memory
The caller method pauses execution at the call site and waits for the callee to return
The caller method continues executing concurrently on another thread
The caller method restarts from line 1
questions.explanation: In standard synchronous Java execution, the caller method pauses at the call site until the callee finishes and returns.

questions.prompt: Can a user-defined method call another user-defined method in the same class?
options: No, only main() is allowed to invoke methods
Yes, any method can invoke any other visible method
Only if they have the exact same parameter types
Only if they have the word 'Helper' in their name
questions.explanation: Methods can freely call each other. This is the cornerstone of modular functional decomposition.

questions.prompt: If both methodA() and methodB() declare a local variable named 'int total', what happens?
options: A compile-time error occurs due to duplicate variable name
They share the exact same memory address and overwrite each other
Each variable exists independently within its own method scope without conflict
The first method to run deletes the other variable
questions.explanation: Local variables are scoped strictly to the method in which they are declared. Identical names in different methods do not conflict.

questions.prompt: In the expression 'int res = doubleValue(square(3));', which method executes first?
options: doubleValue executes first
square(3) executes first, and its return value (9) is then passed into doubleValue
Both execute at the exact same millisecond
Neither executes until printed
questions.explanation: Inner nested method calls evaluate first. square(3) evaluates to 9, so doubleValue(9) is subsequently invoked.

questions.prompt: What is 'functional decomposition' in software engineering?
options: Deleting unused functions before deploying
Breaking a complex algorithm into smaller, focused helper methods that collaborate
Converting all functions into while loops
Crashing a server by memory exhaustion
questions.explanation: Functional decomposition is the architectural process of breaking a complex task into smaller, modular sub-tasks.

questions.prompt: What happens if methodA calls methodB, and methodB tries to access a variable declared inside methodA?
options: methodB accesses it automatically
A compile-time error occurs: cannot find symbol, because local variables are out of scope
methodB reads it as 0
Java prompts the user on the console
questions.explanation: Method B cannot access Method A's local variables directly. The only way Method A can share data with Method B is by passing it as an argument.

questions.prompt: What is the return value of 'Math.min(Math.max(5, 12), 20)'?
questions.explanation: Math.max(5, 12) evaluates to 12. Then Math.min(12, 20) evaluates to 12.

questions.prompt: Can a method call itself in Java?
options: No, Java explicitly forbids recursive calls
Yes, this is known as recursion
Only inside try-catch blocks
Only if marked with @Self keyword
questions.explanation: A method calling itself is recursive, a fundamental programming technique supported by Java.

practice.title: Helper Method for Cubing Numbers
practice.problemStatement: Write a method 'square(int n)' returning n * n. Then write 'cube(int n)' that calls 'square(n)' and multiplies the result by n. In main(), print the cube of 4.

interviewQA.question: How does execution control transfer between caller and callee in Java?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: When a method call occurs, the caller's execution is paused at that exact line. The runtime evaluates arguments, places them onto a newly created stack frame for the callee, and directs the instruction pointer to the callee's first statement. When the callee returns, control and the return value transfer back to the caller's paused position.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: Can two methods share a local variable without passing it as an argument?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: No. Local variables exist only within the method stack frame where they are declared. To share data, the caller must pass it as an argument, or the data must be stored in a class-level (static) or instance-level field.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: What is method chaining and composition?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Method composition occurs when the return value of one method call is passed directly as an argument to another method (e.g. Math.sqrt(sq(x))). Method chaining occurs when a method returns an object reference on which another method is immediately invoked (e.g. str.trim().toUpperCase()).
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: What is the danger of circular method calls (methodA calls methodB, and methodB calls methodA)?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Circular calls without a terminating condition create an infinite recursion loop. Stack frames keep accumulating on the Call Stack until memory is exhausted, throwing a java.lang.StackOverflowError.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: Why is functional decomposition considered essential in clean code?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Functional decomposition breaks large monolithic logic into small, single-responsibility methods. This makes methods readable, reusable, independently testable, and easier to debug.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: How does Java determine which method to call when names are similar?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Java's compiler checks the method name, number of arguments, and argument types at compile time. It matches the call against the most specific signature available.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

interviewQA.question: What happens if a callee method throws an unhandled exception?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: If an unhandled exception occurs inside a callee, execution aborts immediately. The exception propagates up the call stack to the caller. If no caller in the stack catches the exception, the thread terminates and prints a stack trace.
keyPoints: Focus on memory lifecycle and compile-time contract enforcement.

activities.title: Self-Mastery Checklist
checklist: Caller vs Callee: The caller initiates the invocation and pauses; the callee executes and returns the result.
Method Delegation: Methods can freely invoke other methods to break complex problems into smaller subproblems.
Scope Isolation: Local variables in different methods are completely isolated from one another.
Method Composition: The output of one method can serve directly as the input argument to another method.
Stack Traces: When errors occur, Java prints the exact chain of inter-method calls leading up to the failure.
